newsitem.title: NORWAY: Amoco buy out of Norway Pelican falls through.
newsitem.headline: Amoco buy out of Norway Pelican falls through.

text.p: Shareholders in Norwegian group Pelican AS have declined a takeover offer by oil company Amoco Norway, a statement on the Oslo bourse said on Tuesday.
In September Amoco said it had agreed to take over Pelican and thereby gained equity production stakes in the North Sea Ula and Gyda oilfields.

Pelican owns four percent in the British Petroleum Co Plc operated Gyda field and five percent in Ula. It also holds interests in exploration licences on the Danish continental shelf, close to Amoco's Valhall and Hod oilfields on the Norwegian continental shelf.

"Since the (Norwegian) Finance Ministry cannot accept the transaction on terms acceptable to the owners of Pelican AS, the owners have unanimously decided not to go through with the sale to Amoco," the bourse statement said.

Pelican was established in 1971 and is owned by Selvaag Invest AS (38.2 percent), Norsk Hydro Produksjon AS (35.8 percent), Belships Company Ltd Skibs AS (10.4 percent), Actinor Olje AS (10.2 percent) and Kvaerner Rosenberg AS (5.4 percent).
